$comment: Image CVE exceptions (ADR-0015 item 4). Each entry: id, image (postgres|keycloak|redis|caddy|otelcollector, or the release images api|bff|migrator, #119), package, justification (20+ chars), issue (#n), added and expires (YYYY-MM-DD, expires at most 90 days after added). Matching is exact. A component on the request path of a LAN-reachable service (Caddy, Keycloak and its Java libraries, the BFF, the Api) needs Marco's recorded approval, a reachability argument and an expiry of at most 30 days; Caddy has no exception without it (#120, G3 S-120-07). See docs/runbooks/ci-security-gates.md.

exceptions.justification: CVE-2026-91403, java-21-openjdk-headless 1:21.0.13.0.9-1.2.el9 in the Keycloak 26.8.1 image (sha256:3f3c5f8e03c6..., build 26.8.1-2, Ostium baseline O-035): the OpenJDK CA store trusts roots that signed eMudhra intermediates with weak private keys (CWE-295); fix state: wont-fix, so no package update ends this entry before its expiry. Grype rates it Critical; Red Hat CVSS 3.1 is 6.8 (preliminary) AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N. This package is the JVM that serves Keycloak and it is loaded. Its default trust store is the system ca-certificates store (Red Hat's statement for the RHEL OpenJDK RPMs). In the same Grype database (built 2026-11-08) this image no longer matches CVE-2026-114406 for ca-certificates, which 26.7.5 does; this entry still rests on reachability alone. Keycloak trusts the store as a TLS client (KC_TRUSTSTORE_PATHS adds the Caddy root to it and does not replace it); browsers do not use this store. Deployed context (#120, ADR-0018 D2): Keycloak is on the internal idp and pg-kc networks only; Caddy admits the LAN to /realms/decisya* and /resources/* on 8443 and the workstation to the admin paths on 8444, and port 9000 is never routed; the stack is not deployed today, and the deploy gate refuses while Keycloak's bundled guava (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94) has no fixed release (ADR-0022, D-008). Reachability: Keycloak's only outbound TLS peer is the back-channel logout call to the app host, which resolves to Caddy's fixed address on the internal idp network; JDBC to Postgres is plaintext on the internal pg-kc network, so no CA store is involved; the realm has no identity provider, no SMTP server and no client JWKS URL; Keycloak has no network with egress. A man in the middle needs a position on idp, which holds only Caddy and Keycloak (both with all capabilities dropped, NET_RAW included), or root on the Docker host, and either is already a compromise of the identity tier. Void if any of these changes: any egress network for Keycloak, any outbound peer outside idp and pg-kc, or an identity provider, SMTP server or client JWKS URL in the realm. Keycloak is on the request path of a LAN-reachable service, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: issue #268, approved by Marco 2026-11-08; added 2026-11-08, expires 2026-12-08, 30 days. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-119373, sqlite-libs 3.34.1-11.el9_8 (rpm) in the Keycloak 26.8.1 image (sha256:3f3c5f8e03c6..., build 26.8.1-2, Ostium baseline O-035): Grype rates it High; fix state: not-fixed. sqlite-libs is an operating-system library of the image's base. Reachability (G4 evidence on this digest, docker run --network none, recorded in docs/ai/pipeline/268.md): the started Keycloak JVM maps no libsqlite3, and no file under /opt/keycloak bundles an SQLite library or JDBC driver; Keycloak's store is Postgres over JDBC on the internal pg-kc network, so no request to Keycloak reaches SQLite code. Void if the Keycloak JVM or any provider JAR loads SQLite, or if the bind-mount table admits a provider JAR. Keycloak is on the request path of a LAN-reachable service, so under G3 S-120-07 the approval is recorded here: issue #268, approved by Marco 2026-11-08; added 2026-11-08, expires 2026-12-08, 30 days. CVE-2026-4738, zlib 1.3.2-r1 (Alpine apk) in the Postgres 18-alpine image (sha256:123b17998cca..., pushed 2026-11-06 01:09:38 UTC): Grype rates it Critical; Alpine fix 1.4-r0; affected code: the advisory (Grype's record) names the frmts/zlib/contrib/infback9 modules, program file inftree9.c, that is zlib's optional contrib inflateBack9 and inflate_table9 code. The latest official 18-alpine rebuild, this digest, does not carry the fix, so ADR-0015 item 3 applies while the tag resolves to it; the pin moved here under a one-off cooldown waiver recorded by Marco on 2026-11-09 for the libcurl and brotli-libs fixes, and that rebuild does not fix this finding. Reachability (G4 evidence on this digest, docker run --network none, recorded in docs/ai/pipeline/265.md): the shipped /usr/lib/libz.so.1.3.2 (108376 bytes) contains no inflateBack9 and no inflate_table9, only zlib's standard inflateBack, so the affected contrib code is not compiled into the image's libz and no caller can reach it. The files linking libz.so are postgres, pg_dump, pg_dumpall, pg_restore, pg_basebackup, pg_receivewal, pg_recvlogical, pg_verifybackup, pgcrypto.so, pgxml.so, llvmjit.so, libpq-oauth-18.so, libxml2, libxslt, libexslt, xsltproc, libcurl, LLVM and apk. In PostgreSQL 18 the server reaches zlib only for server-side base-backup compression, which needs the REPLICATION attribute, and through pgcrypto's PGP functions, which need the extension; WAL and TOAST compression never use zlib. Every Decisya role is created NOSUPERUSER and NOREPLICATION (deploy/postgres/init/10-keycloak-db.sh, deploy/postgres/init/20-decisya-db.sh and the migration runner), apart from the bootstrap superuser used only by the init scripts; the repository creates no extension (no CREATE EXTENSION in deploy/ or src/); no stack service runs pg_dump, pg_restore or pg_basebackup. Postgres sits on the internal pg-app and pg-kc networks only and publishes no port; the stack is not deployed today, and the deploy gate refuses while Keycloak's bundled guava (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94) has no fixed release (ADR-0022, D-008). Void if any stack role gains REPLICATION or SUPERUSER, if a migration or init script creates an extension that compresses or decompresses data (pgcrypto included), if a backup service runs pg_dump or pg_basebackup against the stack, or if the server reaches the affected zlib code on any other path. Ends when the tag is rebuilt with the fix; bump the digest then. Issue #265, approved by Marco 2026-11-09; added 2026-11-09, expires 2026-12-09, 30 days. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-4738, zlib 1.3.2-r1 (Alpine apk) in the Redis 8.10.3-alpine image (sha256:7958cfbb9d15..., index pushed 2026-11-11 21:05 UTC, Redis 8.10.3, Alpine 3.23.8): Grype rates it Critical; Alpine fix 1.4-r0; affected code: the advisory (Grype's record) names the frmts/zlib/contrib/infback9 modules, program file inftree9.c, that is zlib's optional contrib inflateBack9 and inflate_table9 code. The tag 8.10.3-alpine resolves to this index digest (read two ways on 2026-11-20: the Docker Hub tags API and the registry Docker-Content-Digest; 8.10-alpine is the same digest), so no fixed official rebuild exists and ADR-0015 item 3 applies while that holds. History: under #265 the pin moved from the index 615b4ced... to 8.10.2-alpine (sha256:9f8d2d789b9a...); under #325 it moved to this digest, the patch tag upstream still rebuilds (8.10.2-alpine was last pushed 2026-10-26). Reachability, class (a), not loaded (G4 evidence on this digest, docker run --network none, recorded in docs/ai/pipeline/325.md; the earlier digest's evidence is in docs/ai/pipeline/265.md): the shipped /usr/lib/libz.so.1.3.2 (108376 bytes) contains no inflateBack9 and no inflate_table9, only zlib's standard inflateBack, so the affected contrib code is not compiled into the image's libz and no caller can reach it. Neither redis-server nor redis-cli links libz.so (redis-server links libzstd, libssl, libcrypto and musl; redis-cli links libssl, libcrypto and musl). The stack keeps the image entrypoint, which loads the image's four bundled modules (redisbloom.so, redisearch.so, redistimeseries.so and rejson.so) whenever it starts redis-server; none of the four links libz. The only files in the image that link libz are /sbin/apk and libapk.so, which the stack never runs (read-only root filesystem, every capability dropped). Redis compresses with its own LZF code, and the stack disables persistence (no RDB, no AOF). Redis sits on the internal cache network only and publishes no port, with the BFF as its only client; its ACL grants the BFF session commands only (no DUMP, RESTORE, MODULE, CONFIG or module command), the default user is off and the health user may only PING. The stack is not deployed today (deploy gate shut by Keycloak's guava, ADR-0022, D-008). Void if redis-server, redis-cli or any loaded module links or maps libz, if the stack loads a module other than these four, if a module command is granted to any enabled ACL user, or if any service runs a program inside the Redis container that uses zlib. Ends when the tag is rebuilt with the fix (Dependabot proposes the digest bump). Issue #265, approved by Marco 2026-11-09; added 2026-11-09, expires 2026-12-09, 30 days. Rewritten in place for this digest under #325; Marco approved the rewrite on 2026-11-20. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

CVE-2026-95691, libssl3 3.5.9-r0 (Alpine apk, upstream openssl) in the Redis 8.10.3-alpine image (sha256:7958cfbb9d15..., Redis 8.10.3, Alpine 3.23.8): Grype rates it High; fix state unknown for Alpine 3.23 (matched by NVD CPE, OpenSSL fixed in 3.5.10). Affected code: the OpenSSL QUIC client's CRYPTO frame retransmission handling (use after free); only a QUIC client talking to a malicious QUIC server. Reachability, class (b), loaded but the vulnerable path is not reached (G4 evidence on this digest, docker run --network none, recorded in docs/ai/pipeline/325.md): redis-server links libssl and libcrypto because the image is built with TLS support, but TLS 1.2 and 1.3 never use AES-GCM-SIV, and Redis performs no CMS encryption and runs no QUIC client. The stack keeps the image entrypoint, which loads the image's four bundled modules (redisbloom.so, redisearch.so, redistimeseries.so and rejson.so) whenever it starts redis-server; redisearch.so and redistimeseries.so also link libssl and libcrypto, and redisbloom.so and rejson.so do not. No binary or module in the image other than libssl and libcrypto imports CMS_encrypt, CMS_encrypt_ex or the OpenSSL QUIC client, and neither redis-server, redis-cli nor any of the four modules contains the GCM-SIV cipher name. The stack's redis.conf and Compose service set no tls- option (S-120-12 guard). Redis sits on the internal cache network only and publishes no port, with the BFF as its only client; its ACL grants no module command to any enabled user (the default user is off, the health user may only PING, and the BFF has a fixed list of session commands). The stack is not deployed today (deploy gate shut by Keycloak's guava, ADR-0022, D-008). Void if redis-server, redis-cli, a loaded module or any other process in the container imports CMS_encrypt, CMS_encrypt_ex or the OpenSSL QUIC client or uses AES-GCM-SIV, if the stack loads a module other than these four, or if a module command is granted to any enabled ACL user. Ends when a Redis image with OpenSSL 3.5.9-r1 or later is pinned. Issue #325, approved by Marco 2026-11-20; added 2026-11-20, expires 2026-12-02. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

No binary or module in the image other than libssl and libcrypto imports CMS_encrypt, CMS_encrypt_ex or the OpenSSL QUIC client, and neither redis-server, redis-cli nor any of the four modules contains the GCM-SIV cipher name. The stack's redis.conf and Compose service set no tls- option (S-120-12 guard). Redis sits on the internal cache network only and publishes no port, with the BFF as its only client; its ACL grants no module command to any enabled user (the default user is off, the health user may only PING, and the BFF has a fixed list of session commands). The stack is not deployed today (deploy gate shut by Keycloak's guava, ADR-0022, D-008). Void if redis-server, redis-cli, a loaded module or any other process in the container imports CMS_encrypt, CMS_encrypt_ex or the OpenSSL QUIC client or uses AES-GCM-SIV, if the stack loads a module other than these four, or if a module command is granted to any enabled ACL user. Ends when a Redis image with OpenSSL 3.5.9-r1 or later is pinned. Issue #325, approved by Marco 2026-11-20; added 2026-11-20, expires 2026-12-02. Not renewed past this expiry without a new issue and a fresh G3.

GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q (CVE-2026-116587), github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 v3.0.5 in the Caddy v2.11.7 binary of the self-built image (the pinned ghcr.io/mpcs2013/decisya-caddy image and every build from deploy/caddy/image): denial of service when parsing JWKs that contain RSA keys (High, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). No fixed v3 release exists (fix state: not-fixed, v3.0.5 is the latest), and no Caddy release drops v3 (v2.11.9 of 2026-11-05 still requires v3.0.5); v4 is raised to 4.1.6 under ADR-0021 item 3 (#212). Remove when a fixed v3 or a Caddy release without v3 exists. Component path: caddypki, then smallstep authority, then go.step.sm/crypto/jose, linked into the binary. Class (b), the vulnerable path is not reachable in the deployed configuration (G3 ruling 1 of #212, re-checked under #265): tls internal signs a certificate request made in-process, with no token and no JWK from a peer; Caddy's internal issuer builds the smallstep authority with no provisioners, and only the acme_server directive configures provisioners, which the Caddyfile does not use; the admin API is off; every site uses the internal issuer only; no other standard module verifies JOSE. The #265 overrides (golang.org/x/net v0.62.0, github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.2) leave the module set (modules.txt) and this path unchanged. Void at once, whatever the expiry, if any of these changes: an acme_server directive or a pki CA other than the implicit local one; the admin API turned on in any form; a TLS issuer other than internal, or Caddy as an ACME client; a module added to the build that verifies JWS or JWT or fetches a JWKS; a Caddy bump that changes the component path above. Impact if a premise failed: availability only, on the LAN edge before authentication. Caddy is the LAN edge, so under G3 S-120-07 and ADR-0021 item 7 the approval is recorded here: first accepted 2026-10-29 under #212; renewed under issue #265, approved by Marco 2026-11-09; added 2026-11-09, expires 2026-12-09, 30 days. A further renewal needs a new issue, a fresh G3 and a fresh approval.
